statements.label: thm:main
statements.statement_latex:
[Principal theorem]\label{thm:main}
The confined pair $(\cw,\cs)$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Both comparisons are decidable on all finite ordinary typed inputs.
\item The weak part is reflexive and transitive. The strict part is
transitive and well founded, is included in the weak part, and satisfies
$\cw\,;\,\cs\subseteq\cs$ and $\cs\,;\,\cw\subseteq\cs$.
\item Both parts are preserved by every original well-typed context and
every type-preserving capture-avoiding substitution by ordinary terms.
\item Every original beta, case and recursor reduction is strict.
\item On the first-order $\mathcal F$-algebra, $\cs$ is exactly multiset
recursive path ordering for the chosen precedence.
\item Every individual descending strict rank is below $\BH$, and
\[
 \sup_s\bigl(\rk_{\cs}(s)+1\bigr)=\BH.
\]
An effective family of closed native T terms of outer type $o\to o$
already has cofinal ranks; $\mathcal F$ is unnecessary for this lower bound.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: lem:sharp-syntax
statements.statement_latex:
[Refinement syntax]\label{lem:sharp-syntax}
The relation $\sharpens$ is reflexive and transitive. It commutes
with renaming, opening, and simultaneous substitution by
pointwise refining environments. It preserves retyping of a
marked root and reflects a successful partial mark:
\[
 q\sharpens s,\quad \mk(s)=s'
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mk(q)=q'\text{ and }q'\sharpens s'
 \quad\text{for some }q'.
 \tag{M}
\]
Suppose $q\sharpens s$ and $a_i\sharpens b_i$ in corresponding
types. If $\ap s{\vec b}$ succeeds, then $\ap q{\vec a}$ succeeds
and its result refines the result on the right.

Let $\vec a,\vec b$ be lists of prefix copies of one marked
owner $P$. Suppose
\[
 \ap q{\vec a}=r,\qquad \ap r{\vec b}=w.
\]
Then either $\ap q{\vec a,\vec b}=w$, or $P\sharpens w$,
at the output type of $w$.

possibly by an empty path and modulo finite equivalence, to $\tr(t)$.

positive. Consequently, for ordinary confined endpoints,
\[

 \tr(s)R_{\Ty(s)}\tr(t).
\]

statements.label: thm:main
statements.statement_latex:
[Comparison classification]\label{thm:main}
There is an explicit permitted primitive recursive control \(f_*\) for
which the following hold, uniformly in a supplied computable admissible
literal parsing policy.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Universal canonical weak comparison, strict comparison and equality
are decidable for original T terms all of whose free variables have ground
type. Bound variables, result types, internal types, and recursors are
unrestricted.
\item Universal canonical weak and strict comparison are undecidable for
ground-output terms with free-variable levels at most one and internal
type levels at most two, by a finite-query reduction.
\item The negative result has a single-query reduction when internal
type levels at most three are allowed.
\end{enumerate}
For every supplied \(b\), the same assertions hold for an explicit
control \(f_b\) equal to \(G\) on \([0,b]\) and satisfying
\(0\le f_b(n)-G(n)<2\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n)\) thereafter.

equalities and congruences over finite circuits of fixed-head collapses
are decidable. The procedure preserves shared inputs and shared circuit
nodes. The fixed heads may be arbitrary ordinals below \(\varepsilon_0\).

statements.label: thm:counts
statements.statement_latex:
[Uniform complete-count residues]\label{thm:counts}
For every \(m\ge1\) and every nonzero limit \(\lambda\), put
\(T=\max\{N(\lambda),m,B_f\}\).  For all \(t\ge T\),
\begin{align*}
 \lambda\ge\omega^2:\quad&
 D_\lambda(t)\equiv p(t)\pmod m,\quad
 Z_\lambda(t)\equiv0\pmod{2m},\quad
 J_\lambda(t)\equiv p(t)\pmod m;\\
 \lambda=\omega k:\quad&
 D_\lambda(t)=k,\quad
 Z_\lambda(t)\equiv2p(t)-2k\pmod{2m},\quad
 J_\lambda(t)\equiv2p(t)-k\pmod m.
\end{align*}
In particular, the first line gives a period \(2m\) and the explicit
table \(r\mapsto\lfloor r/2\rfloor\bmod m\) for every head
\(\lambda\ge\omega^2\).

statements.label: prop:entry-residues
statements.statement_latex:
[Entry tables]\label{prop:entry-residues}
Put \(c_\nu=\lceil N(\nu)/2\rceil\).  On a computable tail,
an interval of the form \(\lambda=\nu+\omega k\), \(k\ge1\),
has \(\tau(t)=k\) and \(E(t)=f^k(t)\).  Every other proper interval
has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:long-entry-residues}
 \tau(t)\equiv p(t)-c_\nu\pmod m,\qquad
 E(t)\equiv2c_\nu\pmod{2m}.
\end{equation}
A sufficient tail for these formulas is
\(t\ge\max\{N(\lambda),N(\nu)+3,m,B_f\}\).

statements.label: lem:propagation
statements.statement_latex:
[Propagation]\label{lem:propagation}
If \(V_{i+k}>U_i=\rho>0\) and
\(b'_{i+k+1}\ge b_i+S\), then
\(V_{i+k+1}\ge\rho>U_{i+1}\).
If instead \(V_{i+k}=U_i\) and
\(b'_{i+k+1}\ge b_{i+1}+S\), then
\(V_{i+k+1}\ge U_{i+1}\).
For equal next budgets the latter conclusion also follows from
\(s'\le s\) on all eligible candidates.

statements.label: lem:gap-input
statements.statement_latex:
[Gap and input comparison]\label{lem:gap-input}
For two fixed intervals \(P,Q\), put
\(S=\max\{1,N(\mu_P),N(\mu_Q)\}\). On effective tails:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If \(\delta_P>\delta_Q\), then
\(\tau_P(t)>\tau_Q(t)\) and \(E_P(t)>E_Q(t)\).
\item If \(\delta_P\ge\delta_Q\) and \(t>u\), then
\(\tau_P(t)\ge\tau_Q(u)\) and \(E_P(t)>E_Q(u)\).
\item For fixed \(k\ge1\), if
\(\delta_P\ge\delta_Q+\omega k\) and \(u+S\le f^k(t)\), then
\(\tau_P(t)\ge\tau_Q(u)+k\) and \(E_P(t)>E_Q(u)\).
\end{enumerate}

\(q>R+2\), while their whole-state leading exponent, and hence their
two distinct shifts \(c<c'\), remain fixed. Their limit parts diverge

statements.label: lem:norm-arithmetic
statements.statement_latex:
[Effective ordinal operations and norm bounds]
\label{lem:norm-arithmetic}
Every norm ball is finite and effectively enumerable.  Cantor-normal-form
comparison, $\oplus$, $\otimes$, and ordinal exponentiation $2^\alpha$
are effective.  Moreover
\begin{align*}
 N(\alpha\oplus\beta)&=N(\alpha)+N(\beta),\\
 N(\alpha)+N(\beta)-1
 &\le N(\alpha\otimes\beta)\le N(\alpha)N(\beta)
       &&(\alpha,\beta>0),\\
 N(\alpha)&\le2N(2^\alpha),\qquad
 N(2^\alpha)\le2^{N(\alpha)}.
\end{align*}

statements.label: lem:collapse-estimates
statements.statement_latex:
[Basic collapse estimates]\label{lem:collapse-estimates}
If $\beta<\alpha$ and $N(\beta)\le f(N(\alpha))$, then
$\psi_f(\beta)+1\le\psi_f(\alpha)$.  For $n,k\in\N$,
\[
 \psi_f(n)=n,\qquad N(\alpha)\le\psi_f(\alpha),\qquad
 \psi_f(\alpha)+k\le\psi_f(\alpha+k).
\]
If $\alpha\ge\omega$, then $\psi_f(\alpha)>f(N(\alpha))$.

statements.label: thm:maximum-predecessor
statements.statement_latex:
[Greedy maximum]\label{thm:maximum-predecessor}
The following simultaneous recursion computes $M$ and $L$ exactly.
Write $\alpha=\omega^e c+r$, where $c>0$ and $r<\omega^e$, and
put $w=1+N(e)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $M(\alpha,0)=0$ and $L(0,b)=L(e,0)=0$.
\item If $r>0$ and $cw\le b$, then
\[
 M(\alpha,b)=\omega^e c+M(r,b-cw).
\]
\item Otherwise set
\[
 d=\begin{cases}
 \min\{c-1,\lfloor b/w\rfloor\},&r=0,\\
 \min\{c,\lfloor b/w\rfloor\},&r>0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then $M(\alpha,b)=\omega^e d+L(e,b-dw)$, with a zero block
omitted.
\item If $e,b>0$, put $a=M(e,b-1)$, $v=1+N(a)$ and
$(q,s)=\operatorname{divmod}(b,v)$.  Then
\[
 L(e,b)=\omega^a q+L(a,s).
\]
\end{enumerate}
statements.reuse_status: requires exact source and dependency comparison

statements.label: lem:limit-saturation
statements.statement_latex:
[Limit saturation and monotonicity]\label{lem:limit-saturation}
For every nonzero limit $\lambda$ and every $b\in\N$,
\[
 N(M(\lambda,b))=b.
\]
For fixed $\lambda$ this maximum is strictly increasing in $b$.
For arbitrary bounds the function $M$ is weakly increasing in each
argument wherever the predecessor interpretation is defined.
statements.reuse_status: requires exact source and dependency comparison

statements.label: thm:single-predecessor
statements.statement_latex:
[Single-predecessor collapse recurrence]
\label{thm:single-predecessor}
For every nonzero limit $\lambda$ and $n\in\N$,
\[
 \psi_f(\lambda+n)
   =\psi_f\bigl(M(\lambda,f(N(\lambda)+n))\bigr)+1.
\]
statements.reuse_status: requires exact source and dependency comparison

statements.label: cor:closed-evaluation
statements.statement_latex:
[Closed evaluation and its norm orbit]
\label{cor:closed-evaluation}
A closed collapse value is computable by the following deterministic
descent.  At a nonfinite state $\alpha=\lambda+n$, replace it by
$M(\lambda,f(N(\alpha)))$ and add one to an event counter.
On reaching a finite state $Z$, return $Z$ plus that counter.
If the initial norm is $t$ and the number of events is $D$, then
\[
 Z=f^D(t),\qquad \psi_f(\alpha)=Z+D.
\]
For a nonfinite initial state one also has $0<D<Z$.
statements.reuse_status: requires exact source and dependency comparison

statements.label: cor:finite-coefficient
statements.statement_latex:
[Finite coefficient identity]\label{cor:finite-coefficient}
For all $k,n\in\N$,
\[
 \psi_f(\omega k+n)=f^k(2k+n)+k.
\]
statements.reuse_status: requires exact source and dependency comparison

statements.label: lem:pair-compiler
statements.statement_latex:
[Signed polynomial pairs]\label{lem:pair-compiler}
Every signed linear expression $D$ in ordinal unknowns with coefficients
in $\mathbb Z[\omega]$ has effectively constructed actual $A_D,B_D:\tau$
whose first-coordinate difference is $2^kD$ for a finite $k$.
All free functional variables have type $\tau$, and internal types have
level at most two.  Differences are taken only in the signed Cantor-monomial
group; each of the two source coordinates remains a positive ordinal.
statements.reuse_status: requires exact source and dependency comparison

statements.label: lem:functional-detector
statements.statement_latex:
[Alignment and a full-vector detector]\label{lem:functional-detector}
At each fixed admissible valuation of the original inputs, the condition
$\can A_1=\can B_1$ is equivalent to the existence of two fresh
positive ground inputs making the full canonical vectors of
\[
 A'=(\lambda t:o.A)z,\qquad B'=(\lambda t:o.B)w
\]
equal.  Full-vector equality of any actual pair of type $\tau$ can in turn
be detected by ground sources $L,R$ satisfying $L_0\ge R_0$, with equality
exactly at vector equality and otherwise gap at least two.

statements.label: thm:functional-hardness
statements.statement_latex:
[Functional-input undecidability]
\label{thm:functional-hardness}
Full universal canonical weak comparison and strict comparison are
undecidable already for ground output, free-variable levels at most one,
and internal levels at most two.  The reduction at this level uses finitely
many comparison queries.  A computable single-query reduction from the
same polynomial-system unsatisfiability problem is available with internal
level at most three.

and single-query internal level bound three.

If $a,b\in C$ have bounded norm and $\lv(a)>\lv(b)=n$, then
$a\square b$ belongs to $C$ and has bounded norm.  The same statement

statements.statement_latex:
[Finite definition and substitution covariance]
\label{lem:source-finiteness}

 &\le N(\alpha\otimes\beta)\le N(\alpha)N(\beta)

$\psi(\beta)+1\le\psi(\alpha)$.  For $n,k\in\N$,

statements.label: f:thm:maximum-predecessor
statements.statement_latex:
[Greedy maximum]\label{f:thm:maximum-predecessor}
The following simultaneous recursion computes $M$ and $L$ exactly.
Write $\alpha=\omega^e c+r$, where $c>0$ and $r<\omega^e$, and
put $w=1+N(e)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $M(\alpha,0)=0$ and $L(0,b)=L(e,0)=0$.
\item If $r>0$ and $cw\le b$, then
\[
 M(\alpha,b)=\omega^e c+M(r,b-cw).
\]
\item Otherwise set
\[
 d=\begin{cases}
 \min\{c-1,\lfloor b/w\rfloor\},&r=0,\\
 \min\{c,\lfloor b/w\rfloor\},&r>0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then $M(\alpha,b)=\omega^e d+L(e,b-dw)$, with a zero block
omitted.
\item If $e,b>0$, put $a=M(e,b-1)$, $v=1+N(a)$ and
$(q,s)=\operatorname{divmod}(b,v)$.  Then
\[
 L(e,b)=\omega^a q+L(a,s).
\]
\end{enumerate}

statements.statement_latex:
[Closed evaluation and its norm orbit]
\label{f:cor:closed-evaluation}

descent.  At a nonfinite state $\alpha=\lambda+n$, replace it by

If the initial norm is $t$ and the number of events is $D$, then
\[

[Uniform kernel separation]\label{m:lem:uniform}

$T_d=\max(T_{d-1},100C_{d-1}+100d)$. For $d\ge3$, $c,e\ge0$, signed

[Permitted growth and a bounded perturbation]

on $[0,b]$. It satisfies
\[
 0\le\Gamma_b(n)-G(n)\le1,\qquad
 G(n)\le\Gamma_b(n)<G(n+1),\qquad
 \Gamma_b(n+1)\ge2^{2^{\Gamma_b(n)}}.

with only ground free variables and ground binders, prime constants

comparison on terms with ground free names, of arbitrary result type,
are co-recursively-enumerable. This comparison problem is decidable if
and only if there is a total computable function $b(Q)$ such that
every false query $Q$ has a countervaluation with every raw ground
coordinate at most $b(Q)$.

such that
\[
 F_j(n)\equiv r_m\pmod m\quad(j\ge1, n\ge m).

statements.label: prop:actual-attainment

with its actual canonical vector $(c_H,a_H)$. Put
\[
 \lambda=\omega\otimes a_H,\qquad

statements.statement_latex:
[Main results]\label{thm:main}
The constructions below have the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $d,m\ge1$, let $p_d(n)$ count partitions of $n$ with parts at most $d$, and
put $Q_d=d!m^{d-1}$. A complete deletion of one $\omega^d$ suffix
with retained mass $c\ge0$ and initial total norm at least $c+d+1$
has event count congruent to $p_d(S-c)$ modulo
$m$, whenever every operational budget is at least the current norm
and is congruent to $S\ge c$ modulo $Q_d$.
\item For each fixed $d$, the binary coefficients of
$\prod_{i=1}^d(1+z^i)^{-1}$ are computed exactly by two explicit
linear maps on a space of dimension $d(d+1)/2$ over $\Ftwo$.
Distinct numerator states have distinguishing continuations of length
at most $\lceil\log_2(d(d+1)/2)\rceil$.
\item After an explicit finite transient, the complete residue profile
is closed under both binary selectors. At a pole $\zeta$ its two
updates are $b_\zeta\mapsto b_\zeta^{1/2}$ and
$b_\zeta\mapsto(\zeta b_\zeta)^{1/2}$; the scalar output is
$\sum_\zeta b_\zeta/\zeta$.
\item For every $v\ge4$, the descent from
$\omega^{\omega+1}+(v-4)$ has an explicit first
$\omega^\omega$-block parity. On its linked partition parameters,
a primitive-root residue tuple has exact period
$2(\log_2 B-1)$, where $B=G(G(v))$.
Every eventual period of the complete differential Cartier state
is divisible by this number.
\end{enumerate}

[A complete residue-profile observer]
\label{thm:residue-observer}
Proper rational differentials over $\Ftwo$ with simple poles
in $\mathcal R_d$ correspond bijectively to $\mathcal P_d$ by
\[
 R(z)\,dz=\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal R_d}
                 \frac{b_\zeta}{z-\zeta}\,dz.
 \tag{PF}
\]
The profile space is finite and is closed under both binary
transitions. At each fixed pole their updates and the output are
\[
 \mathcal L_1:\ b_\zeta\longmapsto b_\zeta^{1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathcal L_0:\ b_\zeta\longmapsto(\zeta b_\zeta)^{1/2},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{out}(b)=\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal R_d}
                             \frac{b_\zeta}{\zeta}\in\Ftwo.
 \tag{U}
\]
After the finite transient of
Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-transient}, this is an exact observer
for every remaining binary continuation.

[Greedy predecessor]\label{thm:greedy}
The following simultaneous recursion computes $M,L$ exactly.
Write $\alpha=\omega^e c+r$ with $c>0$, $r<\omega^e$, and
$w=1+\norm(e)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $M(\alpha,0)=0$ and $L(0,b)=L(e,0)=0$.
\item If $r>0$ and $cw\le b$, then
\[
 M(\alpha,b)=\omega^e c+M(r,b-cw).
\]
\item Otherwise, put
\[
 a=\begin{cases}
 \min(c-1,\lfloor b/w\rfloor),&r=0,\\
 \min(c,\lfloor b/w\rfloor),&r>0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then $M(\alpha,b)=\omega^e a+L(e,b-aw)$.
\item If $e,b>0$, put $\eta=M(e,b-1)$,
$v=1+\norm(\eta)$ and $(q,s)=\operatorname{divmod}(b,v)$.
Then $L(e,b)=\omega^\eta q+L(\eta,s)$.
\end{enumerate}
Zero blocks are omitted.
